newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely softer on Friday, dealers said.
"The market opened with a surplus today and everyone is busy trying to place their money," commented one.
Dealers said the central Reserve Bank had already auctioned Z$400 million worth of treasury bills in the market at 17.59 percent, to squeeze off the excess liquidity.
At Thursday's weekly treasury bill tender, the central bank sold off Z$55 million worth of the 91-day paper at a rate of 17.60 percent.

Meanwhile on Friday, bankers acceptances were quoted at 18 an 17.75 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18.25 and 17.75 percent while NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought and sold at 18.50 and 18.25 percent respectively from 19 and 18.25 percent.
Call money was indicated at 17.75 percent from 18.50, in a market which closed on Thursday with a Z$334 million surplus from Z$210 million on Wednesday.
